title: LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's git-file lock has no heartbeat and no push-verification, causing near-miss double-claims (GH-526 stale-TTL, GH-518 push-visibility-lag)
registered_by: ORCH (r-co-2-loop session, observed live during GitHub-issue loop mode on 2026-08-07/08)
related_to: docs/anti-patterns.md GH-542 incident (2026-08-07) -- the original 'push immediately' rule this issue extends

GH-526 -- workspace r-co-1-loop's lock aged past TTL_MINUTES (120) while still actively committing every few minutes; a second workspace's gh_claim.py correctly-per-the-old-rule reclaimed it. No double-run occurred only because the original run finished and merged moments later.

GH-518 -- workspace r-co-1-loop committed a claim locally, pushed its own feature branch, and (evidently) began Step 00 work, all without the claim commit reaching origin/main. A second workspace's gh_claim.py, reading a main that still showed GH-518 unclaimed, was handed the same issue. Detected manually via a branch-existence check before any WF-03 work started on the second workspace; as of filing, still unresolved on origin/main after 20+ minutes, suggesting the first workspace's session may have stalled entirely.
scope: docs/agents/protocols/LOOP_PROTOCOL.md, tools/gh_claim.py, tools/queue_heartbeat.py (new) -- the GitHub-issue loop's distributed locking mechanism.
symptom: Two related but distinct near-miss double-claim incidents in one session, both correctly avoided only through manual intervention rather than protocol enforcement: (1) GH-526 -- a lock legitimately claimed and still actively worked was reclaimed by a second workspace purely because wall-clock time since the ORIGINAL claim exceeded TTL_MINUTES (120), with no mechanism for the original claimant to signal ongoing activity. (2) GH-518 -- a workspace's claim commit existed locally and on its own feature branch but had not reached origin/main; gh_claim.py, whose only source of truth is origin/main, correctly reported the issue as unclaimed to a second workspace, which was handed the same issue.
root_cause_analysis: The lock registry (handoffs/global_queue.json, committed to git) has two structural gaps relative to what a distributed lock needs: (1) No heartbeat/lease-renewal mechanism -- TTL_MINUTES exists purely to reclaim locks from workspaces that died or stalled, but the only recorded timestamp (locked_at) is set once, at claim time, and never updated for the lock's remaining lifetime, so 'genuinely still working, just slow' and 'dead 120+ minutes ago' are indistinguishable by wall-clock alone. (2) No push-verification gate -- LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's existing 'PUSH THE CLAIM TO MAIN IMMEDIATELY' step was advisory prose (do X, then do Y) with no explicit instruction to READ BACK the pushed ref and confirm it landed before proceeding to Step 00 (git-setup, which itself pushes a new branch and is easy to treat as sufficient forward progress without having actually confirmed the queue claim's own push succeeded).
impact: Both incidents this session resolved themselves without an actual double-run (GH-526's original claimant finished first; GH-518 was caught manually before any WF-03 work started on the second workspace), but neither outcome was guaranteed by the protocol as written -- both were near-misses that succeeded by timing luck, not by design. A future occurrence under less favorable timing (e.g. two workspaces both reaching Step 03 BACKEND-DEV before either notices) would produce genuinely wasted work, conflicting commits on the same GitHub issue, and duplicate PRs.
acceptance_criteria: A heartbeat mechanism exists (queue_heartbeat.py) that a workspace can call periodically during a long WF-03 run to signal ongoing activity, without disturbing the lock's original locked_at audit timestamp
gh_claim.py's staleness check considers the heartbeat timestamp (when present) instead of the original claim timestamp, so a workspace sending regular heartbeats is never reclaimed by TTL alone
LOOP_PROTOCOL.md documents an explicit 'read back the pushed ref' verification step between pushing a claim and proceeding to Step 00, not just 'push and continue'
LOOP_PROTOCOL.md's Invariants checklist reflects both new requirements
The fix does not require a new coordination service or infrastructure -- stays within the existing git-committed-JSON-file lock design, per explicit user direction
evidence_file: Live observation during r-co-2-loop's GitHub-issue loop session on 2026-08-07/08 -- see handoffs/orchestrator.log entries around LOOP_ITEM_CLAIM for WF03-GH521-20260807 (workspace r-co-1-loop) and the surrounding timeline; GH-518's claim commit (b11d309 on feature/WF03-GH518-20260808) never reached origin/main during the observation window (~20+ minutes).
notes: User explicitly scoped the fix to stay within the existing git-file lock design rather than building a separate coordinator service, after being presented both options. This issue and its fix are themselves the direct result of a loop-mode session pausing GitHub-issue processing to address a protocol gap discovered mid-session, per the Unblock-Everything directive's spirit (a genuine blocker to safe continued operation) even though it required stepping outside a single WF-03 issue-resolution run.
resolution: Added tools/queue_heartbeat.py: refreshes lock.heartbeat_at (leaving lock.locked_at untouched, preserving its audit meaning) for an item the calling workspace still owns; rejects if the item isn't found, isn't locked by the caller, or isn't IN_PROGRESS. Updated gh_claim.py's staleness check to use lock.heartbeat_at when present, falling back to lock.locked_at when a lock has never been heartbeated -- verified via direct logic test (3 cases: stale/no-heartbeat -> expired; stale-locked_at/fresh-heartbeat -> NOT expired; stale-locked_at/stale-heartbeat -> expired) and an end-to-end functional test against a scratch queue file (heartbeat recorded correctly, locked_at preserved, wrong-workspace/not-found/not-IN_PROGRESS rejections all verified). Updated LOOP_PROTOCOL.md: added an explicit 'VERIFY THE PUSH LANDED' step (git fetch + git log --oneline -1 origin/main showing the claim commit) between pushing a claim and proceeding to Step 00, added a 'HEARTBEAT DURING LONG RUNS' step documenting the new tool and cadence, added queue_heartbeat.py to the Tools reference section, and updated the Invariants checklist to require both the push-verification and periodic-heartbeat practices explicitly rather than leaving them as unenforced prose.
